newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: TWO BULGARIANS ESCAPE FROM SOUTH AFRICAN JAIL.
newsitem.headline: TWO BULGARIANS ESCAPE FROM SOUTH AFRICAN JAIL.

text.p: Three of South Africa's most wanted criminals -- one sought for at least 16 murders and two Bulgarians who ran a multi-million dollar car theft syndicate -- escaped from police custody this week, police said on Saturday.
Spokesman Captain Jan Combrinck said gang leader Josiah Rabotapi disappeared two days after he was arrested, while being transported under maximum police security from court back to jail in Pretoria.

"Rabotapi established a dangerous armed robbery syndicate about a decade ago. He is wanted for about 16 murders and more than 30 armed robberies worth about 70 million rand ($16 million). He has escaped police custody twice in three years," Combrinck told Reuters.

The Saturday Star newspaper quotes sources as saying Rabotapi ran his syndicate, which is behind much of the criminal activity in the "crime capital" of Johannesburg, like an army camp with drills and secret meetings in safe houses.
Police have nicknamed Rabotapi Mr Fingers after he lost his thumb and forefinger in a shootout with them last year.

In a separate escape, two Bulgarian nationals Ivan Pramatarov and Ognyan Ognyanov, arrested on January 23 with 14 other Bulgarians in connection with a car theft syndicate, escaped from a prison in Johannesburg on Tuesday.
Spokesman Captain Jan du Toit said two men, carrying false police identification, pretended to be police detectives who came to fetch the felons from prison for further investigation. ($1=4.43 rand)
